findings.claim: In SpanFlusher.join(), when the deadline expires the `break` exits the per-process loop before terminate() runs for the current and remaining flusher processes, leaving them running after join returns during shutdown/rebalance.

verifier.reason: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:337-347, when the deadline expires (remaining_time <= 0), the break at lines 340-341 exits the loop before process.terminate() at lines 346-347 runs for the current and remaining processes. As a result, those flusher processes are left running when join() returns during shutdown or rebalance.

findings.claim: The isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard before process.kill() in the restart path (_ensure_processes_alive) is always False for spawn-context SpawnProcess objects, so hung or unhealthy processes are never killed before replacements start. The pre-PR code called kill() unconditionally.

verifier.reason: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:53,105, worker processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process (returning SpawnProcess, a sibling of multiprocessing.context.Process under BaseProcess), so isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) at src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:254 is always False. As a result, process.kill() at line 255 is never executed before _create_process_for_shards() starts a replacement at line 259, whereas the pre-PR code called self.process.kill() unconditionally.

findings.claim: In join(), terminate() sits behind the same isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) check, which is always False for SpawnProcess, so flusher processes are never terminated on shutdown or rebalance.

verifier.reason: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:53,105, flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process (SpawnProcess), which is a sibling of multiprocessing.context.Process under BaseProcess, so isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) in join() at flusher.py:346-347 is always False and process.terminate() is never called. However, this isinstance check in join() was pre-existing before the patch (previously isinstance(self.process, multiprocessing.Process)).

findings.claim: _create_process_for_shard (lines 127-132) has no callers in src/ or tests/ and only delegates to _create_process_for_shards, so it is dead code.

verifier.reason: SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard at src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:127-132 is newly introduced by this patch and only looks up the shard in self.process_to_shards_map to call _create_process_for_shards. Both _create_processes (line 84) and _ensure_processes_alive (line 259) call _create_process_for_shards directly, and no callers of _create_process_for_shard exist in the patch or tests.

findings.claim: The docstring 'Creates one process per shard' does not match the default deployment, where the CLI default of 1 runs all shards in one process. The comments at lines 178 and 235 also do not match the code.

verifier.reason: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:32 claims 'Creates one process per shard for parallel processing', whereas src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:432-437 defaults --flusher-processes to 1, causing SpanFlusher (flusher.py:51,60-66) to cap num_processes at 1 and run all shards in one process. Likewise, flusher.py:178 describes updating healthy_since 'for all shards' even though line 179 updates a single per-process Value, and flusher.py:235 says 'Check if any shard handled by this process is unhealthy' inside an elif body that only sets cause = 'hang' (line 236) after checking the single per-process healthy_since value (lines 231-234).

findings.claim: The spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce timer (line 199) uses tag key 'shards', while the other metrics in the same flush loop (lines 185, 195, 244) use 'shard'.

verifier.reason: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:199, the spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce timer passes tags={"shards": shard_tag}, whereas the other metrics added by this patch at flusher.py:185, flusher.py:195, and flusher.py:244 (in _ensure_processes_alive) use the singular tag key "shard".
